stances_toward.note: ECOWAS suspended Guinea after the coup of 5 September 2021 (BBC, 9 September 2021). Guinea stays in the bloc and cooperates on the file out of necessity, with visible friction: reluctant_partner is our reading of that structure (C); no source uses the word. Bond none: pure interest, nothing sourced underneath. Gap: whether the suspension was lifted after the 28 December 2025 election is not verified in this pass.

stances_toward.note: ECOWAS suspended Guinea-Bissau from its decision-making bodies after the coup of 26 November 2025, and its mediators (Bio, Faye) then took part in talks with the junta. The junta cooperates in the talks and resists the bloc's terms (a short, structured transition): reluctant_partner is our reading (C); no source uses the words. Trend cooling from the suspension. Bond none is our reading. Gaps: the 2025 withdrawal of the ECOMIB stabilisation force and whether the suspension has been lifted are not verified in this pass.

stances_toward.note: Rival: the junta left ECOWAS (announced 28 January 2024, effective 29 January 2025) after the 2022 sanctions and the 2012-era embargo history cited in its own sources. Exit is not a will to destroy the bloc, so not adversary. Bond grievance is our reading of the sanctions episode; the sources describe the exit as a sovereignty move.

stances_toward.note: Nigeria's regional instrument and, as a founder and its largest member, its paymaster: treaty-based membership (ecowas.int member list), a standby-force roadmap for a 1,650-strong counter-terrorism brigade endorsed again at the Freetown summit (July 2026; operational July 2027, activation estimated at EUR 2.26bn, ISS), and a Tinubu chairmanship of the Authority until June 2025. Graded ally on the structural position (founder, treaty membership, the same bloc whose sanctions it drove), not on a source using the word, so C; the ECOWAS mutual-defence protocol was not opened. Stable rather than warming: Tinubu sent his vice president to Freetown, Senegal's Faye now chairs the Authority, and the bloc has lost three members, which is the culminating-point risk the Currents page watches for. Mirror: the Mali card reads ECOWAS as rival/grievance after the sanctions; the Nigerian side of that quarrel is the NER and org-aes stances. Bond affinity: the shared-institution tie, no kinship named. The since-date is the start of the 2023 chairmanship and the Niger sanctions episode, not the founding of the bloc.
